items.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: And then once I got to Rutgers University, studying with Ralph Bowen, I learned, I was coming from a major/minor world.

ctx.x: Did it help that, I would guess in your classical study you had learned your scales. So that must have helped when you go to figure out the chords. Right?

Definitely. Definitely. And then once I got to Rutgers University, studying with Ralph Bowen, I learned, I was coming from a major/minor world. That’s all. It was like major, minor, maybe a diminished. Like that’s all I really knew about. And he opened my ears and my mind up to a whole world of sound and sound possibilities through building them in a scale. And I still go back to it. You play it but it’s good to go back to it and just like study it again. Because then it comes out a different way. Because you’re…
Yeah. Evolution, and your “I got it” moment with your chords, did you have a similar moment with your career or was it more of a gradual, maybe I can do this?
